# PID tuning rules

Notebooks: 04. Primary experiment file: `exp_04_pid_tuning_comparison`.

| Source | Status | Role | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ziegler, J. G.; Nichols, N. B. (1942). Optimum settings for automatic controllers. Transactions of the ASME, 64, 759-768. | verified | Origin of the open-loop (reaction curve) and closed-loop (ultimate gain) PID rules. | Tuned for a pneumatic controller and quarter-amplitude decay; the loops are often oscillatory by modern criteria. |
| Cohen, G. H.; Coon, G. A. (1953). Theoretical consideration of retarded control. Transactions of the ASME, 75, 827-834. | partial | Reaction-curve tuning rules that account for large dead time. | Rules are for quarter-amplitude decay; the title is cited with small wording variants in the literature. |
| Tyreus, B. D.; Luyben, W. L. (1992). Tuning PI controllers for integrator/dead time processes. Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Research. doi:10.1021/ie00011a029. | partial | Source of the Tyreus-Luyben ultimate-point rules (less oscillatory than Z-N). | Developed for PI on integrator plus dead time processes; use for PID is an extension in common practice. |
| Rivera, D. E.; Morari, M.; Skogestad, S. (1986). Internal model control: PID controller design. Industrial & Engineering Chemistry Process Design and Development, 25(1), 252-265. doi:10.1021/i200032a041. | verified | Derives PID settings from the IMC procedure with one tuning parameter. | Model based; assumes a reasonably accurate low-order model. |
| Skogestad, S. (2003). Simple analytic rules for model reduction and PID controller tuning. Journal of Process Control, 13(4), 291-309. doi:10.1016/S0959-1524(02)00062-8. | verified | SIMC rules and the half rule for effective delay. | An erratum exists (J. Process Control 14, 2004, p. 465). |
| Astrom, K. J.; Hagglund, T. (1984). Automatic tuning of simple regulators with specifications on phase and amplitude margins. Automatica, 20(5), 645-651. doi:10.1016/0005-1098(84)90014-1. | verified | Relay feedback experiment for estimating the ultimate gain and period. | The describing-function estimate is approximate for non-sinusoidal limit cycles. |
| Astrom, K. J.; Hagglund, T. (1995). PID Controllers: Theory, Design, and Tuning, 2nd ed.. ISA (Instrument Society of America). ISBN 1-55617-516-7. | verified | Standard reference on PID structure, anti-windup, filtering and tuning. | Pre-dates much current autotuning practice. |
| Seborg, D. E.; Edgar, T. F.; Mellichamp, D. A.; Doyle, F. J. (2016). Process Dynamics and Control, 4th ed.. Wiley. ISBN 978-1-119-28591-5. | verified | Process-control textbook: FOPDT models, reaction-curve methods, tuning rules. | Which tuning rules and identification methods it covers was not checked page by page in this build. |

## Limitations recorded in the experiment

- FOPDT plants only, one K and T; four L/T values.
- Rule formulas transcribed from commonly published forms; not checked against the original papers.
- Frequency-domain margins ignore the derivative filter and sampling delay.
- No noise, saturation, or hardware validation.
